newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima says no NATO entry while neutral.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima says no NATO entry while neutral.

text.p: Austria's Social Democrat Chancellor Viktor Klima, in conflict with his conservative coalition partners, on Tuesday ruled out NATO membership as long as Austria remained neutral.
"I know of no experts who say that neutrality and NATO are compatible," he said in a statement after a weekly cabinet meeting.
Austria was not under any time pressure and should wait and watch new developments in the military alliance, he added.
Klima's comments directly contradicted the stand of People's Party leader and Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel, who has repeatedly indicated he supports joining NATO.

Schuessel said in an interview with the Standard newspaper this week that entry to NATO would not breach Austrian law on neutrality as long as no foreign troops or nuclear weapons were stationed on Austrian territory.
His party was in favour of telling NATO early this year that Austria was interested in joining the alliance under certain circumstances, he said.
Austria, straddling the former Cold War border between the East and West blocs, has been neutral since 1955, when it drew up its post-World War Two constitution.

The Soviet Union, which occupied Austria after the war with allies Britain, France and the United States, demanded Austria enshrine neutrality in its national charter before it agreed to withdraw its troops.
